**Prefix caching reuses computation only when the preceding context is genuinely the same.** A cached block identifies its tokens together with the parent block's identity and relevant extra inputs. The parent chain ensures that identical token text under different earlier context is not treated as equivalent. [1](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/prefix_caching/)

Stable instructions and examples placed before changing request content can create reusable prefixes. A timestamp near the beginning can prevent reuse of many later blocks even when most text is unchanged.

**A cache hit skips some prefill work, not generation.** New prompt suffixes and new output tokens still require computation. Model versions, adapters, multimodal inputs, and isolation requirements must be represented in the cache identity where relevant.

Measure reused-token fraction, eviction, routing, and actual prefill latency. A prompt layout cannot guarantee a 90% hit rate without a repetitive workload and adequate cache capacity. Preserve semantics and authorization boundaries when arranging prompts. Prefix caching is exact computational reuse under matching context, not semantic caching of vaguely similar requests.

**Technical details and references.**

vLLM's prefix cache identifies full KV blocks using token content plus the preceding block's hash and relevant extra inputs, such as adapter or multimodal identity and isolation salt where configured. Chaining the parent hash ensures identical later tokens are reusable only under the same earlier context. A hit skips prefill computation for those matching blocks. [1](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/prefix_caching/)

Put stable instructions/examples before changing queries or timestamps to maximize shared prefixes, while preserving prompt semantics and authorization boundaries. This improves opportunities for reuse but does not guarantee a 90% hit rate: routing, eviction, block alignment, workload repetition, and model/configuration changes matter. Track reused-token fraction, prefill latency, and cache isolation. Prefix caching does not cache arbitrary semantically similar text and does not eliminate the cost of generating new output tokens.
